To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
{\it neural networks (NNs) implement renormalization group theory using information geometry}.
NNs are a special case of S-System, and S-System implements RG.

NNs are a special case of a more general class of algorithms, S-System, that implement RG, which is a special case of the renormalization of information geometry, and that under realistic conditions, large size nonlinear deep NNs with the hinge loss are universal optimizers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following three questions: 1) What is a NN?; 2) How does a NN work?; 3) What is the large scale behavior of a NN?
the theory of NNs, including learning and optimization
the {\it large scale} properties of NNs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
{\it the theory of NNs is the theory of RG}, which has been a central theory in modern physics for decades, and {\it the theory for NN optimization is random matrix theory}.
NNs implement {\bf RG} using {\it information geometry}.
NNs are the most efficient way to learn and solve optimization problems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a theory of NNs that unifies the {\it geometry, learning, and optimization} in the NNs.
NNs are {\it S-Systems} and S-Systems are {\it RGs}.
we provide the first rigorous mathematical foundation for deep NNs, which is a long-standing open problem, and we show that NNs are {\it optimal} for learning, which is a fundamental open problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NNs are {\it not} just a {\it black box} and they have a deep connection to many fundamental mathematical theories.
NNs implement a renormalization group using information geometry, and that deep NNs are universal approximators of any continuous function.
NNs are a special case of the S-System, and that the theory can be applied to a broad class of learning problems, including optimization, machine learning, and deep learning.
